correctness.rationale: The normal form f(i)=1+sum_(j<i) ε_j is bijective. Under composition, each active inner increment addresses a distinct outer Bernoulli variable; the joint probability-generating polynomial factors as product_i(1-pq+pq t_i), proving exact independent output increments for all n and endpoint p,q. Exact uniform tuple fibers, rank binomial, absorption distribution, and cutoff follow by stated finite-count identities and elementary binomial inequalities. A separate direct-composition script exhaustively checks map-valued distributions on n≤6 and products through four factors, but it is not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the full joint increment-law identity μ_p*μ_q=μ_pq for a specific noncommutative finite-chain contraction monoid, giving exact k-factor fiber sizes depending only on output rank and a sharp absorption cutoff. The 2013 same-object full text states one-element height and fixed-point enumeration (Proposition 4.1 and Corollaries 4.4–4.7), not the composition law. The 2022 same-object full text studies Green relations, semigroup rank, generators and natural order, not probabilistic convolution. Targeted published-record and primary-literature searches found no matching statement. Inaccessible broader Higgins 1990/1992 probability-themed sources create a genuine priority limitation, but their abstracts alone do not imply that this special contraction-family convolution is covered.

value.rationale: The product law controls complete random transformations, not merely a marginal invariant: it gives every specified map fiber for every product length and a one-parameter multiplicative convolution submonoid inside a noncommutative semigroup. The exact absorption time and total-variation cutoff at logarithmic depth are natural consequences for iterative random multiplication. These are uniform all-degree classifications motivated by multiplication dynamics and are not a simple restatement of one-map rank counts.
